findings.text: In the configuration without extended page metadata, the subsystem reports itself as unavailable, all initialization operations complete without effect, retrieval by page descriptor or by physical address always indicates absence, and release completes without effect.

The fragment cache provides initialization that places the cache in an empty state, a predicate that reports whether the cached page came from the emergency reserve, and a decoder that inspects the encoded word for the reserve flag.

Folio youth and idleness are exposed as paired operations that fetch associated extended metadata, operate on dedicated flag bits when metadata exists, release the metadata reference afterwards, and degrade to negative or no effect when metadata is absent.

Page ownership tracking has two builds. One build forwards reset, record, split, copy, migration reason update and dump requests to lower level handlers only when a global readiness indicator is active. The other build accepts the same requests and completes without effect.

Reference counting is offered symmetrically for pages and folios with read, assign, increment, decrement, addition and subtraction by an amount, plus variants that return the resulting value or report whether the result reached zero.

Conditional acquisition succeeds only when the current count is nonzero, with single reference and arbitrary count forms. A freeze operation transitions an expected nonzero count to zero and reports success, while unfreeze moves from zero to a caller supplied nonzero value.

Page table checking has two builds. One build forwards allocation, release, single and multiple entry installation at three table levels, and range clearing to lower level handlers unless a global disable indicator is active. The other build accepts the same requests without effect. Single entry installation at two upper levels is defined as multiple installation of one entry.

Compaction skip marking for a pageblock has two builds. One build queries, clears and sets a dedicated skip flag associated with the containing block. The other build reports the flag as always clear and accepts clear and set requests without effect.

Per CPU storage is declared and defined through section parameterized macros with convenience wrappers for the default section, cache hot objects, cacheline aligned and shared aligned objects, and page aligned objects, with attribute handling that differs between two builds.

The reporting device descriptor contains a callback that consumes a scatter list and length and returns a status, a delayed work item for background processing, an atomic state word, a minimum order threshold, and a per batch page limit where zero selects a built in default.
The fragment cache object carries a single encoded word that simultaneously records the retained page and associated allocation attributes, with zero denoting the empty state.
All folio level count operations act on the count stored in the first constituent page, and page level count queries resolve through the enclosing folio, so the two views observe one shared value.
The encoded cache word reserves low order bits for the allocation order and a distinct higher bit for emergency reserve origin, so decoding either attribute does not disturb the other.

Youth and idleness queries return negative and mutating operations return without effect whenever extended metadata lookup indicates absence, preserving safe behavior when the feature is disabled or the folio lacks metadata.
Ownership and table check wrappers perform no observable work unless their respective global branch indicators select the active path; otherwise they delegate to lower level handlers.

A pageblock type is encoded in three low bits, compaction skip uses a separate bit, and isolation when present uses another dedicated bit that preserves the type value. The total bit count exposed externally is rounded up to a power of two with word alignment assumed.
Trace activity probing reports the underlying tracepoint state in one build and always reports inactive in the other, where all trace notification helpers complete without effect.

Count examination and mutation use atomic primitives with release ordering on unfreeze, requiring no caller held lock for the count word itself. Optional trace notifications fire only when their respective tracepoints are active.

Each youth or idleness flag access acquires a metadata reference before touching flag storage and releases it afterwards, so the flag word remains valid across the bit operation without additional locking shown.

A count starts at one, moves by unit or arbitrary steps in either direction, supports conditional increment that fails at zero, supports atomic transition from an expected value to zero with success indication, and supports transition from zero to a supplied nonzero value.
Each of the youth and idleness flags behaves as an independent binary cell with operations to test persistence, assert, clear, and atomically test and clear in one step.

Fragment allocation entry points accept a cache, a size and allocation flags, with one form also accepting an alignment that must be a power of two and is transformed before delegation, and a simpler form requesting default alignment behavior.
The reporting callback and delayed work item form the device facing entry points for converting reclaimed pages into reports and for scheduling background reporting activity.
Unfreeze expects the current count to be zero and the replacement value to be nonzero; violation is treated as a programming error detected by debug checks.
Supplying a fragment alignment that is not a power of two triggers a one time warning, indicating caller error while still delegating the request.
The default maximum pages per reporting batch equals 32, an unspecified reporting order is represented by negative 1, and a configured capacity of zero selects the default.
In one build the order mask covers the low eight bits and in another build it is zero. The emergency reserve flag occupies the value one greater than the mask.

Pageblock size in pages is two raised to a configurable order. Related helpers align a frame number upward, test alignment, round downward to block start, and round upward past a frame to block end. The order itself is the minimum of a huge page order and a maximum in two builds and the maximum alone in a third.
The migratetype mask combines the three type bits. The isolation mask equals the isolation bit in one build and zero in the other.

Shared aligned and aligned section suffixes are empty in one build, a shared aligned suffix in another, and mixed empty plus shared aligned in a third. Cache hot objects use a hot qualified subsection and page aligned objects use a page aligned subsection with page size alignment.
